intro_html: Switzerland's most photographed easy alpine hike: traverse past five glacier-fed lakes—Riffelsee, Stellisee, Grindjesee, and more—with the Matterhorn reflected in crystalline waters at every turn. Accessible via the Gornergrat Railway from car-free Zermatt, this quintessential Valais experience combines accessibility with breathtaking alpine scenery.

routes.title_html: Gornergrat Ridge & Riffelalp Loop — Grade: T2 (Hiking) | Elevation gain: 400 m | Time: 3–4 hours | Distance: ~7 km. Scenic alpine walk from Gornergrat (3,110 m) descending to Riffelalp via the exposed east ridge, returning via Rotenboden to Riffelalp station. Outstanding Matterhorn viewpoint throughout the route. Well-marked, safe trail suitable for mountain-experienced hikers.
bullets_html: Rotenboden railway station (2572m) — Start point; well-marked trailhead
Riffelhorn junction (2928m) — 1.5 hrs; viewpoint with Matterhorn views
Riffelberg hotel (2600m) — 2 hrs from start; rest & refreshment point
Gornergrat trail proper (2900m) — Exposed ridge with cairns; T2 terrain
Hohtälli plateau approach (3085m) — Final approach to summit platform
Gornergrat summit (3135m) — Panoramic platform with 29 peaks visible

getting_there.by_pt_html: By Train: Take the main rail line to Visp or Brig (via Zurich, Bern, or Geneva). Visp to Zermatt: Take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn (MGB) regional train from Visp to Zermatt (1.5 hours, runs hourly). Zermatt to Gornergrat: From Zermatt train station, walk 50 m to the Gornergrat Bahn (GGB) mountain railway station. The rack railway climbs 1,620 m vertically in just 9 km, reaching Gornergrat in approximately 40 minutes. Departures every 20–30 minutes in summer (typically 07:00–16:30, with later departures on clear evenings). Journey time from Geneva: Approximately 4–5 hours total (train + transfers). Swiss Travel Pass / Half-Fare Card: Valid on all mountain railways in the region.
getting_there.by_car_html: From Basel / Zurich / Geneva: Drive via A2/A9 motorway towards Valais. Exit at Visp or Brig, then head south to Zermatt (63 km from Visp, approximately 1.5 hours). Parking in Zermatt: No personal cars allowed in Zermatt village. Leave your car at a parking facility: Parkhaus Zermatt: Large multi-story car park near the train station entrance (CHF 15–20/day). Parking Winkelmatten: Larger lot on the outskirts, slightly cheaper. Free parking: Some spaces available along Bahnhofstrasse early morning (limited, first-come basis). Free shuttle bus runs frequently between car parks and village centre. Walk to Gornergrat railway station (5–10 min) or use electric taxis (Zermatt is car-free).

lapse_rate.example_html: Zermatt +20°C → Gornergrat approximately +5°C (roughly 1°C per 300 m elevation gain). Example: If 20°C in Zermatt, expect 5–8°C on Gornergrat with significant wind chill.

weather.season_html: Best season: June–September. July–August offers the most stable weather and shortest daylight hours are still sufficient for full-day tours. June: Snow possible above 3,000 m, glacier crossings may be risky. July–August: Optimal conditions; high tourist traffic. September: Fewer crowds, reliable weather, still excellent conditions. October onwards: Significant snow, railway may close during storms. Weather hazards: Rapid afternoon thunderstorms (common June–August). Strong föhn winds from south. UV intensity extreme at altitude—bring high-SPF sunscreen. Temperature can drop rapidly; layer clothing. Wind-chill makes conditions feel 10–15°C colder than actual temperature.

takeaways_html: Weather exposure & thunderstorm risk: Ridge is fully exposed above 2900m; afternoon thunderstorms common May–September. Many reports cite turnarounds due to rapid cloud build-up or lightning risk after 14:00.

Crowds & trail congestion: Gornergrat is Switzerland's most-visited 3000m peak; summer weekends very busy. Early starts (07:00–08:00) strongly recommended to avoid afternoon congestion and escape crowds.
Snow/avalanche hazard (shoulder season): May–June: lingering snowfields can obscure trail markers above 2800m. Crampons needed in late spring; some route-finding difficulty in poor visibility.

safety_html: Electrical storm risk (primary): Exposed ridge at 3135m; afternoon convection common; lightning fatalities documented; mandatory retreat if thunder/lightning approach.
Exposure & scrambling: Upper ridge (2900–3135m) = T2 grade; loose scree; unroped but vertically exposed; ~300m cliff drops either side in places.
Weather deterioration: Rapid visibility loss; Swiss Alpine Club reports hypothermia risk even in summer if unprepared for wind/rain.
Crowding & trail conflicts: High-traffic intersection with Riffelalp descent; trail narrowing causes bottlenecks.
Altitude & fitness: 3135m is threshold for mild hypoxia in untrained hikers; cumulative fatigue on descent.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
disclaimer_html: This page is an informal hike plan, not professional mountain-safety advice. Conditions change rapidly. Always check MeteoSwiss and SAC before setting out.
